note:
Every extension name each context advertises, put back through getExtension. Chrome hands back a named interface object per extension. Both arms now agree on all 77 keys -- 75 interface rows plus the two supported lists -- with no difference in brand, prototype member set, member values or arity.

What the first run of this probe (git history, 2026-08-25T02:31) found instead: WebGL 1 answered undefined for 37 of 39, because the union payload was void; WebGL 2 answered [object Object] for 34 of 36, because one anonymous empty struct stood in for all of them -- and its prototype was Object.prototype, so reading the prototype answered __defineGetter__, hasOwnProperty and ten more members no WebGL extension has. getSupportedExtensions listed every name in both arms throughout, so the engine advertised what it then refused.

`values` is the member set per interface: GLenums as the numbers Chrome reports, functions as fn/<arity>. 53 unique interfaces, 213 member slots; an interface advertised by both contexts carries identical members in each. Still short of Chrome: the methods are no-ops, so getSupportedProfiles, getTranslatedShaderSource and isVertexArrayOES have Chrome's arity and not Chrome's return value -- which is why this probe records arity and not return values.

chrome_swiftshader.note: The same Chrome forced onto SwiftShader (--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader), which is the only way to reach OVR_multiview2: the Metal driver above never advertises it, so its interface is the one name in the WebGL 2 union with no reading in the `chrome` section. Only that one row is recorded here -- the rest of a SwiftShader run belongs to a different GPU table. Renderer string this was taken from: ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (LLVM 10.0.0) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver). Its webgl2 list was 30 names against the 29 the linux table in gpu.zig claims; the extra is EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2, which a macOS host's SwiftShader has and the reference Linux one did not. That is a host difference, not a correction to the table.
